title: Break Through Walls
statement: A robot moves on a grid one cell at a time up, down, left or right. Cells with 1 are walls; the robot may break through at most k walls on its way. Return the fewest moves from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, or −1 if it is impossible.
constraints: grid[0][0] and the last cell are 0

answerKey.pattern: BFS over states (row, column, walls left)
keyPoints: A cell alone is not enough: arriving with more breaks left can be better
Each state has up to four neighbours; stepping into a wall uses one break
BFS gives the fewest moves; the first time the target appears, stop
edgeCases: k large enough to walk straight: rows + columns − 2
No route even with k breaks: −1
acceptableSlowerApproaches: BFS on cells only, keeping the first visit: misses routes with more breaks left
Try every set of walls to break: exponential

hints: Why is (row, column) not a complete state here?
Two arrivals at the same cell differ if they have different numbers of breaks left.
BFS on (r, c, left); keep best[r][c] = most breaks left seen, and skip states that are no better.
